trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.
Going around the edge to (1,3) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Number 3 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes around the edge to (1,5).
Going around the edge to (1,1), the next 9 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,3); going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

Contradiction! Going down would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order), and that's the only legal move. So my guess (left from number 5) was wrong, so the line must go down.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Going down, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,1). So the line goes right.
Number 7 is only reachable this way.
The line must go left: right is number 12, which comes later; down is number 13, which comes later.
Going down would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going up would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (2,5) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Cell (4,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
